links.outcome: Effect of fairness-aware losses and ethical-framing prompts on subgroup disparities and accuracy
links.effect: Worst-group loss gave a better performance-fairness balance than fairness-regularized loss. Ethical-framing prompts reduced gender bias in 1-shot only. Neither prompting strategy nor more shots reduced race/ethnicity disparities.
links.quote: Among fairness-aware techniques for mitigating bias in DNN-based embeddings, the worst-group loss, which is designed to minimize loss for the worst-performing demographic group, achieves a better balance between performance and fairness.

links.outcome: Depression detection performance and fairness across gender and race/ethnicity subgroups
links.effect: LLMs showed reduced gender bias compared with DNN embeddings, but racial disparities persisted. LLMs outperformed DNNs particularly for underrepresented groups such as Hispanic participants.
links.quote: LLMs also exhibit reduced gender bias compared to DNN-based embeddings, though racial disparities persist.

unlisted_practices: Ethical-framing guided prompting and increased shot counts in LLMs to mitigate demographic bias

screen.practice: ethical-framing prompt guardrails and fairness-aware loss for bias mitigation
screen.reason: Evaluates fairness-aware prompting and loss functions to mitigate algorithmic bias (gender and race/ethnicity disparities) in automated depression detection using clinical interview transcripts.

primary.practice: guided prompting with ethical framing and fairness-aware loss
